hero.title: LINQ
intro.0: In the Collections lesson you built lists and looped over them by hand to count or find things. LINQ gives you ready-made tools to ask a question about a list - keep only some items, count them, pull out one field, sort them - in one short line instead of a foreach. Each operator takes a lambda - the short `x => ...` rule you wrote in the Lambdas lesson - so you pick the operator and write the rule. Here you write each query yourself and run it: one operator per task - Where, Count, Any, All, Select, FirstOrDefault and OrderBy.
task.1.title: Keep only what matches: Where
task.1.context: Filtering means keeping only the items that pass a test. `Where` takes a lambda - the short inline rule you wrote in the Lambdas lesson. Here `animal => animal.Legs == 4` reads "for each animal, is its Legs equal to 4?". `Where` runs that lambda on every animal and hands back a new sequence of the ones it said true for - no loop to write.
task.1.goal.0: In `FourLegged`, return only the animals whose `Legs` equals 4.
task.1.goal.1: `Main` prints each survivor's name, so the output should be Dog then Cat.
task.2.title: How many match: Count
task.2.context: `Count` does the start-at-zero, loop, check, add-one tally for you. Give it a lambda and it returns how many items passed - a plain number.
task.2.goal.0: In `FourLeggedCount`, return how many animals have exactly 4 legs.
task.2.goal.1: `Main` prints the number, so the output should be 2.
task.3.title: Is there at least one: Any
task.3.context: Sometimes you only need a yes or no: is there at least one item that matches? You give `Any` a lambda; it returns a `bool` and stops the moment one item makes it true.
task.3.goal.0: In `AnyTwoLegged`, return whether any animal has exactly 2 legs.
task.3.goal.1: `Main` prints True or False, so the output should be True.
task.4.title: Do they all match: All
task.4.context: `All` checks the whole sequence: it returns true only when every item passes the lambda. A single failure makes it false.
task.4.goal.0: In `AllHaveLegs`, return whether every animal has more than 0 legs.
task.4.goal.1: `Main` prints True or False, so the output should be True.
task.5.title: Turn each into something else: Select
task.5.context: `Select` reshapes a sequence: it runs a lambda on every item and collects the results. Often you use it to pull out one field - from a sequence of animals to a sequence of just their names.
task.5.goal.0: In `Names`, return each animal's `Name` as a sequence of strings.
task.5.goal.1: `Main` prints each name, so the output should be Dog, Duck, Cat.
task.6.title: The first match, or nothing: FirstOrDefault
task.6.context: `FirstOrDefault` hands you the first item that matches your rule - and when nothing matches, it gives back a default instead of a match (for an object that default is `null`, a value meaning "nothing here"). Reach for it whenever a match might not exist; `Main` here already checks for that default.
task.6.goal.0: In `FirstTwoLegged`, return the first animal with exactly 2 legs, or the default if there is none.
task.6.goal.1: `Main` prints the found animal's name, so the output should be Duck.
task.7.title: Sort by a key: OrderBy
task.7.context: `OrderBy` returns the same items in a new order, sorted by whatever the lambda picks out. Pick the name and they come out alphabetically; pick the leg count and they come out smallest first.
task.7.goal.0: In `ByName`, return the animals ordered alphabetically by `Name`.
task.7.goal.1: `Main` prints each name, so the output should be Cat, Dog, Duck.
task.8.title: LINQ recap
task.8.summaryIntro: Each LINQ operator takes a rule (a lambda) and answers one kind of question about a sequence. Reach for the one that matches what you want back.
task.8.summaryItems.0.title: Where -
task.8.summaryItems.0.text: keep only the items that match; returns a filtered sequence.
task.8.summaryItems.1.title: Count -
task.8.summaryItems.1.text: how many items match; returns a number.
task.8.summaryItems.2.title: Any -
task.8.summaryItems.2.text: is there at least one match; returns a `bool`.
task.8.summaryItems.3.title: All -
task.8.summaryItems.3.text: do all items match; returns a `bool`.
task.8.summaryItems.4.title: Select -
task.8.summaryItems.4.text: turn each item into something else; returns a reshaped sequence.
task.8.summaryItems.5.title: FirstOrDefault -
task.8.summaryItems.5.text: the first match, or a default (like `null`) if there is none.
task.8.summaryItems.6.title: OrderBy -
task.8.summaryItems.6.text: sort the items by the value the rule picks.
task.8.summaryClose: Next in this track: errors and null - handling the cases where things go wrong or a value is missing.
